title: Forensic Evidence: Data Lifecycle, Retention, and Authorization Playbook
author: Anika Rao
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook specifies the standardized lifecycle for forensic evidence used during security incidents at Redwood Inference. It binds RBAC controls, audit logging expectations, data residency/retention requirements, SDLC checkpoints that affect evidence generation, and legal/operations handoff procedures. The goal is to ensure evidence is collected, preserved, and produced with chain-of-custody guarantees and compliance-ready metadata.

Audience: Security Incident Responders, SRE, Legal, Privacy, Product, and Engineering teams operating or supporting hosted/dedicated/private deployments.

Scope: Applies to telemetry and artifacts produced by: authn-service, token-gateway, inference-runtime, auditstream, kvcache-service, evidence-collector, and console-backend. Does NOT replace specific customer contractual obligations; see related customer-specific evidence runbooks.

Key principles
- Immutable capture: Audit and forensics artifacts must be captured in an append-only store (auditstream) with signed sequence numbers.
- Least-privilege access: Evidence access is controlled by tiered RBAC with just-in-time elevation and session recording.
- Residency-aware packaging: Evidence containing customer data must preserve data residency and apply redaction/proxying when evidence is exported.
- Timebound retention with legal hold: Standard retention applies unless a legal hold is declared.

Roles & ownership
- Security IR Lead (owner): Escalates evidence needs, authorizes legal hold. Primary: security-ir@redwood.com
- Forensics Engineer: Runs evidence extraction and validation (owner of evidence-collector). Primary: forensics@redwood.com
- SRE oncall: Provides infrastructure retrieval and storage quotas. Primary: sre-oncall@redwood.com
- Legal and Privacy: Approves disclosure, handles subpoenas. Primary: legal@redwood.com
- Platform Engineering: Operates auditstream and long-term storage. Primary: infra-audit@redwood.com

SLOs & thresholds
- Audit capture latency (auditstream -> cold-store): <= 2 minutes (99th percentile)
- Evidence package export availability: 99.5% monthly uptime for evidence-collector API
- Retrieval SLA for Critical incidents (P0): retrieve and assemble package within 4 hours
- Chain-of-custody integrity check: hash verification must complete within 30 minutes of package creation

Data classification & retention table
| Data class | Examples | Default retention | Cold-store TTL | Residency constraints | Access tier |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Audit logs (system) | authn success/failure, config changes | 18 months | 7 years | Cross-region copies with residency metadata | Tier 2 |
| Request traces (non-PII) | runtime traces, scheduler events | 12 months | 3 years | Global copy allowed | Tier 2 |
| Customer inference payloads (may contain PII) | user prompt, returned tokens | 90 days | 2 years (encrypted, region-bound) | Must not leave customer's region unless approved | Tier 3 (restricted) |
| Secrets & keys metadata | KMS rotation events, key IDs | 2 years (logs only) | 7 years | Never exported in raw form | Tier 1 (restricted) |

RBAC & authorization model for evidence access
- Evidence access is enforced by the Evidence Access Service (EAS). Roles: Evidence-Viewer, Evidence-Forensics, Evidence-Admin.
- Just-in-time elevation: Evidence-Forensics requires an approval token issued by Security IR Lead. JIT token TTL: 2 hours, single-use.
- Session recording: All EAS sessions with Tier 3 evidence are recorded and stored alongside the package with separate retention (7 years).
- Approval workflow: EAS integrates with approval-bot in Slack and with the Audit Policy engine to generate an approval record that feeds into auditstream.

Access matrix (high level)
- Evidence-Viewer: read-only access to redacted packages (automated redaction applied for Tier 3).
- Evidence-Forensics: unredacted access after JIT approval; multi-factor and SSO required.
- Evidence-Admin: config and emergency override; reserved for security leadership and infra-sysadmins. Emergency overrides require post-hoc audit and Legal approval within 48h.

Procedure: Receiving an evidence request during an incident (numbered steps)
1) Incident triage marks evidence-required and assigns Evidence Request ID (ER-<INCIDENT-ID>).
2) Security IR Lead opens a forensics ticket and tags SRE + Forensics Engineer.
3) Forensics Engineer calls evidence-collector CLI to create a package manifest (example below).
4) Evidence-collector pulls data from auditstream (signed segments), runtime, and customer-region cold-store, computes SHA-256 digests for each artifact, and stores an encrypted package in evidence-bucket with a metadata.json manifest.
5) For critical (P0) incidents, Security IR Lead triggers legal hold to prevent TTL expiration.
6) EAS issues access tokens per the JIT workflow; access is recorded in auditstream.
7) After analysis, package state is marked “consumed” or “archived” and retention metadata adjusted.

CLI examples and packaging manifest
- Create package (forensic engineer):
  $ evidence-collector create --incident ER-1234 --scope authn-service,inference-runtime --since 2026-02-10T00:00:00Z --until 2026-02-10T06:00:00Z --region eu-west-1

- Example metadata.json (manifest, excerpt):
  {
    "package_id": "pkg-ER-1234-20260210",
    "created_by": "forensics@redwood.com",
    "components": ["auditstream-segment-20260210-1.log", "runtime-trace-abc123.json"],
    "hash": "sha256:3a7bd6...",
    "residency": "eu-west-1",
    "legal_hold": "active"
  }

Packaging and chain-of-custody checklist
- Verify signed segment sequence numbers from auditstream.
- Compute and record SHA-256 digests for each artifact; store digests in manifest and push manifest to immutable manifest-store.
- Sign the manifest with the evidence-collector signing key; record signature in auditstream.
- Upload encrypted package to evidence-bucket with server-side encryption using customer-bound KMS key if package includes customer payloads.

Legal hold and retention adjustments
- Legal/Hold lifecycle:
  1) Legal issues Hold-Token and notifies Security IR Lead.
  2) Security IR Lead updates package.manifest legal_hold=true and sets retention to indefinite by tagging object metadata: legal_hold:true, hold_id:<token>.
  3) Evidence lifecycle team creates an audit ticket to track hold resolution and required archival steps.
- Removal of legal hold requires Legal signoff and a documented release memo.

Cross-border considerations
- If package contains customer data from a geo-fenced region (e.g., EU/UK), evidence-collector will create a dual-package: (1) primary package stored in customer region; (2) redacted index in global store.
- Export out of region requires: Customer contract exception OR a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) signed by Privacy.

SDLC integration points (how development practices affect evidence quality)
- Feature flags: Any flag change that affects logging must create a telemetry-contract PR that verifies new events are captured in auditstream with schema versioning.
- Release pipelines: Deploys to inference-runtime must include post-deploy trace-sanity checks (automated smoke traces) to ensure evidence continuity.
- Pull Request checklist: Changes touching authn-service or audit schema must include a test demonstrating auditstream messages with the new schema and a migration plan for historical data.

Risk & exceptions framework
- Low-risk exceptions (examples: short-term increased log TTL for debugging) can be approved by SRE lead and logged in the exceptions register for <= 14 days.
- High-risk exceptions (exporting PII outside a region, or disabling signature verification for recovery) require Security + Legal + CTO signoff and automatic escalation to the board-level evidence register.
- Exceptions MUST include: risk rationale, mitigation, rollback plan, and a time-bound expiration.

Audit evidence workflow (end-to-end)
1) Evidence generated by services is emitted to auditstream with schema tags and signed sequence numbers.
2) evidence-collector subscribes to auditstream for incident-scoped ranges and collects correlated artifacts from runtime and cold-store.
3) manifest generation, signing, and upload to evidence-bucket.
4) EAS enforces access controls and records access events back to auditstream.
5) Legal/Security produce packages for external auditors with redaction and supporting attestation statements.

Operational runbook (short checklist for a Forensics Engineer)
- Step 0: Confirm incident ID and classification (P0/P1/P2) and legal constraints.
- Step 1: Run evidence-collector create command and validate manifest hash.
- Step 2: Notify SRE to increase ephemeral storage quota if package > 50GB.
- Step 3: Request JIT access if you need unredacted Tier 3 artifacts.
- Step 4: Produce package and run chain-of-custody verify:
  $ evidence-collector verify --package pkg-ER-1234
- Step 5: Push manifest to immutable-manifest-store:
  $ curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLI_TOKEN" -d @metadata.json https://immutable-manifest-store.internal/api/v1/manifests

Monitoring & metrics (what to watch)
- Unretrieved package age: number of packages older than 30 days with status "ready" (target: < 5)
- Evidence export errors per 1000 requests (target: < 1 per 1000)
- JIT elevation frequency and approval latency (target: < 10 minutes)
- Auditstream capture lag (target: p99 < 2m)

Templates and artifacts (where to find pre-built assets)
- Evidence request template: /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/templates/evidence-request-template
- Manifest schema v2: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/manifest-schema-v2
- Example redaction ruleset: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/redaction-ruleset-2026

Appendix A — Example attestation statement (for auditors)
I, <name>, Forensics Engineer at Redwood Inference, attest that the attached package (pkg-ER-1234-20260210) was produced by the evidence-collector, verified against auditstream sequence numbers, and signed with evidence-collector-signing-key: keyid:ec-sign-2026-01. The manifest and artifacts match recorded SHA-256 digests.

- Forensics oncall: forensics@redwood.com
